clue.text: Memory of crime scene in bombing

indicators.note: bombing blows the words apart, so the letters of crime scene in are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone haunted by the memory of a crime scene during a bombing raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bombing' rearranges CRIME SCENE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A recollection of past events is a memory; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Learn about answer and stupid lies

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: stupid suggests muddled, so the letters of lies are rearranged

explanation.surface: Discovering the truth about an answer full of silly lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' rearranges LIES to LISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to come to understand it, to learn it.

clue.text: Bird's fat under rising batter

indicators.note: under places fat below the reversed piece in the column
in a down light rising means the word for batter is read upwards

parts.note: to lam is to beat or batter
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A duck's fat sitting beneath a rising batter, as in a recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses LAM to MAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The mallard is a common wild duck, a species of bird.

clue.text: Regrets again with lots to turn over

indicators.note: to turn over means to churn the letters of again and lots into a new order

explanation.surface: Regretting once more, with plenty of time to brood over things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn over' rearranges AGAIN and LOTS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a wistful longing for the past, close to regrets about times gone by.

clue.text: Smashing beer, half cut after drink

indicators.note: after puts the halved beer behind the drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: half cut removes half of beer, keeping its second half

explanation.surface: A drinker, half cut after a few beers, calls everything smashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half cut' leaves ER of BEER; 'half cut' is also British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words of praise meaning excellent or wonderful.

clue.text: Sights French tower say, by Seine's left bank

indicators.note: say signals that the tower's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: the Eiffel Tower is the famous Paris landmark

indicators.note: the left bank is the first letter, the left edge of Seine's

explanation.surface: Tourist sights in Paris: the Eiffel Tower by the Left Bank of the Seine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Left Bank is the Paris district south of the Seine; here it is just the first letter, S.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeful is a good long look at something striking, so a sight worth seeing.

clue.text: City's elegance gone

parts.note: chic means stylish elegance
ago means gone by, in the past

explanation.surface: A lament that a city has lost its elegance.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a major US city in Illinois on Lake Michigan.

clue.text: 'Word' for Mac but not Linux?

parts.note: Mac is a word of one syllable, Linux has two; the surface pretends to be about software versions

explanation.surface: Microsoft Word is available for Mac computers but not for Linux.
explanation.walkthrough: The computing surface is the misdirection: the clue is about how many syllables each name has.
explanation.definitionFit: A word of a single syllable describes Mac, but not the two-syllable Linux.

clue.text: Authorities vocal about carbon emissions discharged

indicators.note: about here means the word for vocal goes round the carbon symbol

parts.note: vocal means spoken, oral
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

indicators.note: discharged means emptied, so only the outside letters of emissions remain

explanation.surface: Experts speaking out about carbon emissions being released into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharged' empties EMISSIONS, leaving its outer letters E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Oracles are sources of authoritative wisdom, so experts consulted as authorities fit.

clue.text: Proposition regularly spurned by girl

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of spurned, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: a miss is a young girl

explanation.surface: A marriage proposal regularly rejected by a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of SPURNED: PRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A premiss is a statement assumed in an argument, a proposition from which a conclusion follows.

clue.text: Underground taken from nearest urban settlement

indicators.note: settlement suggests settling into a new arrangement, so the letters of nearest urban are reordered

explanation.surface: An underground railway line taken out from the nearest town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' rearranges NEAREST URBAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Subterranean means existing below the surface of the ground.

clue.text: Part of Beaverbrook in a war's campaign

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Lord Beaverbrook, the wartime press baron and minister, playing a part in a military campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: The battle for the Japanese island in 1945 was a major Pacific military campaign of the Second World War.

clue.text: Rubbish resistance by centre turned supporter

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
a hub is the centre of activity

indicators.note: turned means the word for supporter is flipped round

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A footballer who was a stalwart in the centre of defence switches allegiance, and the fans call it nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses BRA to ARB.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is informal British slang for nonsense or rubbish talk.

clue.text: Abandon maidenly fluttering ditching man

indicators.note: fluttering stirs the letters up, so the word maidenly is rearranged once the other word is taken away

explanation.surface: A coy, fluttering maiden walking away from her suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditching' removes M, A and N from MAIDENLY, and 'fluttering' rearranges the remaining IDELY.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield ground is to give it up, so yield and abandon share the sense of surrender.

clue.text: Good chaps with sound Prime Minister

parts.note: chaps are lads
a tone is a musical sound

explanation.surface: Decent chaps of sound judgement serving under a Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: William Gladstone was the Victorian Liberal leader who served four terms as British premier.

clue.text: Made bitter perfect, judged imbibing beer's head

parts.note: ace means perfect or excellent

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the word for judged takes in the head of the beer

parts.note: rated means judged or assessed

indicators.note: head takes the first letter of beer's

explanation.surface: A beer judge turned sour by a perfect pint's head.
explanation.walkthrough: B goes into RATED after its R: R-B-ATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To acerbate is to embitter or make sour, so its past form means made bitter.

clue.text: Get allies to restore order

indicators.note: to restore is to put back together, so the letters of get allies are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A call to recruit allies to bring back peace and order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restore' rearranges GET ALLIES; the definition is the verb 'order'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass laws is to decree, or order, how people must behave.

clue.text: Ship's grand age with everybody on board

indicators.note: on board means taken inside, so everybody goes in between grand and age

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
an eon is an age
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A grand old ship of an age when everyone was aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon is a large sailing ship of the 15th to 17th centuries.

clue.text: Shock found the French being supportive

indicators.note: in a down light the supporting piece sits underneath, so the French article goes below

parts.note: to found is to start something
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Shock at finding the French unexpectedly supportive.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle someone is to give them a sudden shock or fright.

clue.text: One gives name in entrance

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for name inside the word for entrance

parts.note: a door is an entrance

explanation.surface: Someone giving their name at the entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactor is one who gives, whether money, blood or organs.

clue.text: Top lifted on girl creates embarrassment

indicators.note: in a down light lifted means the word for top is read upwards

parts.note: a lid is a top
Emma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl's top lifted, causing embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' reverses LID to DIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is an awkward predicament, and embarrassment can mean a difficult situation of that kind.

clue.text: Report receiving medal in offensive

indicators.note: receiving means the word for report takes in the medal

parts.note: a report is a loud bang, a noise
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A news report about a soldier receiving a medal during a military offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like a military push but is the adjective; OM is the British Order of Merit.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means unpleasant and disgusting, especially of smells, so it is a synonym of offensive.

clue.text: Capital is firm following endless alarm

indicators.note: following puts the word for firm after the trimmed alarm
endless cuts off the last letter

parts.note: a bell sounds an alarm
fast means firm, as in held fast

explanation.surface: A capital city's company that keeps going after the alarm never stops ringing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims BELL to BEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Belfast is the capital city of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Mostly the drink producing monotonous drone

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: Drinking most of the night, producing a dull droning voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrum is a continuous low humming sound, a steady drone.

clue.text: Target centre, one touching gold perhaps

parts.note: the bull is the centre of a dartboard or target
I is the Roman numeral one
on means touching, as in resting on

explanation.surface: An archer's arrow hits the bull, touching the gold ring at the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: In archery the centre of the target is the gold, which strengthens the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullion is metal in bars, and gold is an example, signalled by perhaps.

clue.text: Opening to escape canopy top in plane, alternatively

definitions.text: Opening to escape canopy top in plane, alternatively

indicators.note: the opening to a word is its first letter, taken from escape
in puts the top of canopy inside the word for plane

parts.note: a jet is a plane

indicators.note: top takes the first letter of canopy

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A pilot's ejection: blasting through the canopy to escape the plane.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the device: an ejector seat fires the pilot out through the canopy of a jet.
explanation.definitionFit: An ejector seat throws the pilot clear of a stricken aircraft, opening the way to escape.

clue.text: Vault over line facing a fair game

parts.note: a burial vault is a tomb
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: An athlete vaulting over a line in a fair contest.
explanation.walkthrough: A tombola is a raffle drum game at British fetes and fairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a lottery stall found at a fete or fair, so it is a fairground game.

clue.text: Mean time retained in stir

indicators.note: in stir means being stirred up, so the letters of time retained are mixed

explanation.surface: A spiteful prisoner held in jail for his time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' is slang for prison, but here 'in stir' rearranges TIME RETAINED.
explanation.definitionFit: A mean is a middle value, and something intermediate lies in between.
